newsitem.title: CHINA: Stolen China explosives stored near nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Stolen China explosives stored near nuclear plant.

text.p: China has arrested a man for stealing explosives that were stored near the Qinshan nuclear power plant in an eastern province.

Wang Quanmin was arrested in October for the theft of 24 kg (53 lb) of explosives taken from a warehouse within 500 metres of the Qinshan nuclear plant, said an edition of Nanjing Weekend available in Beijing on Monday.
The little known newspaper, published in the eastern city of Nanjing, said the explosives were taken in April from a warehouse for quarry materials in Zhejiang province.
Wang, 32, had tried to extort 100,000 yuan ($12,000) from the managers of the warehouse, the newspaper said.
He was detained by police because of a prior criminal record and he confessed under questioning, it said.
It did not say what type of explosives were taken but said they were powerful enough to demolish a tall building.
Qinshan is China's first domestically designed and built commercial nuclear power station. It has been described as the prototype for future development of the nation's nuclear power industry.
Chinese officials have been quoted as saying they took great care in ensuring safety at the plant, which is in a heavily populated area not far from the major city of Shanghai.
